papers.title: PDE-State Conditioning for Learned Optimization Using Physics-Informed Neural Networks
papers.summary: Physics-informed neural network (PINN) optimization depends on global properties of the underlying PDE and how the physics residual evolves across the domain. Standard optimizers such as Adam use fixed gradient-based statistics, while learned PINN optimizers replace the fixed rule with a learned update built from local parameters and optimization-history features. However, none explicitly use PDE-level information. We study two coupled design questions: what PDE-level information should a learned optimizer observe, and how should that information influence its update? We introduce an 11-dimensional PDE state-capturing operator structure, residual geometry, and short-horizon update response, and use it to condition a structured meta-learned optimizer through bounded feature-wise modulation. Repeated design studies identify the compact residual-geometry state G2 and bounded FiLM as the strongest overall choices among those tested. The resulting PDE-State-conditioned optimizer improves all evaluation metrics (relative-L2, L1, solution MSE, and physics MSE) over Adam and the unconditioned learned optimizer on Linear Advection, KdV, and Burgers.
papers.title_ja: 物理情報ニューラルネットワークを用いた学習済み最適化におけるPDE状態条件付け
papers.summary_ja: 物理情報ニューラルネットワーク（PINN）の最適化において、標準的なAdamや既存の学習済み最適化器がPDEレベルの情報を明示的に利用していない問題を解決する手法を提案する。PDEの構造や残差幾何学、短期間の更新応答を捉える11次元の状態オペレータを導入し、これを特徴量ごとの有界なモジュレーション（FiLM）を通じてメタ学習済み最適化器に条件付けする。線形輸送、KdV、Burgers方程式の検証において、このPDE状態条件付け最適化器は、Adamおよび無条件の学習済み最適化器と比較して、相対L2誤差、L1誤差、解のMSE、物理MSEのすべての評価指標で性能向上を示した。
papers.relevance_reason: PINNとメタ学習最適化の融合で、ユーザーの関心である物理情報NNとML手法の組み合わせに直結する。

papers.title: When and why can integral constraints improve the accuracy of physics-informed neural networks?
papers.summary: Adding constraints obtained by integrating governing equations to the loss has been reported to improve the accuracy of physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) in several applications, but mathematical understanding of these benefits remains limited. For several partial differential equations (PDEs), we derive stability estimates for losses with and without integral constraints. The comparison reveals that in certain parameter regimes, the standard loss has very weak control over specific error components, and that the integral constraints restore uniform control of these components. This explains when and why the constraints improve accuracy. Finally, numerical experiments support this interpretation. In parameter regimes where the standard loss is predicted to have weak control over those components, the two losses indeed show clear differences in accuracy. Conversely, in regimes where the standard loss retains sufficient control, both losses yield similar accuracy.
papers.title_ja: 積分制約が物理情報ニューラルネットワーク（PINN）の精度を向上させる条件と理由
papers.summary_ja: 物理情報ニューラルネットワーク（PINN）において、支配方程式の積分制約を損失関数に追加することで精度が向上する現象の数学的メカニズムを解明した。偏微分方程式（PDE）に対する安定性推定を導出し、標準的な損失関数が特定の誤差成分に対して制御が弱いパラメータ領域が存在することを示した。積分制約はこの制御を均一に回復させることで精度向上を実現する。数値実験により、理論的な予測と実際の精度改善が一致することが確認された。
papers.relevance_reason: PINNの理論的裏付けと精度向上手法であり、サロゲートモデルの核心

papers.title: PSTO: A PDE-structured transport operator with shared implicit updates for multiscale CDR systems
papers.summary: Multiscale convection-diffusion-reaction (CDR) systems couple spatial transport with local stiff reaction kinetics, making their numerical simulation computationally demanding. Conventional neural surrogates require costly coupled CDR training data, and their parameter counts scale with the number of transported variables, limiting scalability to high-dimensional CDR systems. Here we propose a PDE-Structured Transport Operator (PSTO) that learns convection--diffusion dynamics solely from reaction-free data. By embedding the PDE structure into the neural architecture, PSTO generalizes to full CDR systems at inference without retraining. A single transport operator block is shared across all transported variables and refined through relaxed fixed-point iterations, performing an implicit-like correction in latent space. This improves stability during recursive multi-step prediction without adding trainable parameters. We evaluate PSTO on three benchmarks: a canonical 2D CDR system, a multiscale Robertson counterflow flame, and a multiscale hydrogen planar jet flame. In every case, PSTO reduces the mean relative $L_2$ error after 100 coupled steps by at least 50% compared to the strongest neural baseline. Ablation studies on the fixed-point iterations and detailed error decomposition further confirm that PSTO achieves both high one-step accuracy and long-term stability in coupled rollouts. Time-step sensitivity analysis shows that PSTO maintains accuracy even with a tenfold larger time step, whereas baseline accuracies decay rapidly as the time step increases. This framework enables efficient, modular modeling of multiscale CDR dynamics by separating transport learning from the treatment of local kinetics.
papers.title_ja: PSTO: 多スケールCDRシステムのための共有暗黙的更新を備えたPDE構造輸送演算子
papers.summary_ja: 多スケール対流・拡散・反応（CDR）系の数値シミュレーションを高速化するため、PDE構造を埋め込んだニューラルオペレータ「PSTO」を提案する。反応なしのデータのみで輸送ダイナミクスを学習し、推論時に反応項を統合することで、高次元系へのスケーラビリティと再学習の不要さを両立させる。共有された輸送ブロックと固定点反復による暗黙的補正により、長期間の再帰予測における安定性を向上させる。ベンチマーク評価では、既存のニューラルベースラインと比較して100ステップ後の平均相対L2誤差を50%以上低減し、タイムステップサイズに対する頑健性も示した。
papers.relevance_reason: 物理情報ニューラルネットとサロゲートモデルによるPDE解法の高速化・安定化に直結する。

papers.title: PWLNet: A Framework for Linearized Neural Surrogates in Nonlinear Process Optimization
papers.summary: Neural networks represent nonlinear process systems accurately, but embedding them in optimization is difficult because smooth activations introduce nonlinear, nonconvex constraints. PWLNet is a Python framework for building optimization-compatible neural surrogates through exact and piecewise-linear reformulations. It combines baseline and physics-informed training, optimization-aware pruning, and Pyomo embeddings based on ReLU mixed-integer linear models, exact tanh nonlinear models, PWL-tanh formulations, and binary-free SOSX branch-and-LP. PWL-native training uses the same activation in training and embedding, avoiding extra linearization error. It is evaluated on Boston housing, the Williams-Otto process, the Van de Vusse reactor, and a hydroformylation semi-batch reactor. On Boston housing, SOSX training gave the best common-architecture model (test MAE 1.984, R2 = 0.925). On Williams-Otto, pruning 15% of hidden neurons reduced MILP solution time 6.5-fold while preserving the selected operating point. For the Van de Vusse reactor, a physics-informed ReLU RNN pruned from 32 to 12 hidden units enabled tractable exact MILP embedding and a 4% true-plant economic gain over the best ramp-and-hold policy, while terminal-aware shrinking-horizon prediction reached 99.7% of the direct-shooting reference. For the hydroformylation reactor, one-step exact-tanh IPOPT reached 99.2% of the certified reference product with peak pressure 20.002 bar (limit 20 bar) and 14.36 s total solve time over 280 moves; ReLU and PWL-native controllers achieved comparable recovery, with ReLU fastest. Longer horizons and physics-informed training did not consistently improve closed-loop results. Overall, compact linearized neural surrogates enable accurate, tractable optimization in steady-state and dynamic applications, with constraint fidelity identified as a key direction for improvement.
papers.title_ja: PWLNet: 非線形プロセス最適化における線形化ニューラルサロゲートのフレームワーク
papers.summary_ja: 非線形プロセスシステムを最適化に組み込む際の非凸制約問題を解決するため、ニューラルネットワークを正確な線形または分段線形モデルへ変換するPythonフレームワーク「PWLNet」を提案する。ReLUやtanh活性化関数を用いた最適化対応のサロゲートモデル構築、物理情報学習、および最適化認識型プルーニングを統合し、Pyomoとの連携を通じてMILPやNLPとして効率的に解けるようにする。ボストン住宅価格、Williams-Ottoプロセス、Van de Vusse反応器、水素化反応器などのケーススタディで、計算時間の大幅短縮と経済性・収率の向上を実証した。特に、コンパクトな線形化サロゲートにより、定常・動的プロセス双方で高精度かつ実用的な最適化が可能になることを示している。
papers.relevance_reason: サロゲートモデルと最適化の高速化が核心であり、ユーザーの関心と高度に一致

papers.title: LLM Complexity: Towards a Computational Complexity View of Large Language Model Inference
papers.summary: Computational complexity theory offers a principled framework for characterizing the efficiency of computational problems, and Large Language Models (LLMs) can similarly be viewed as computational systems executing a structured process of input, inference-time compute, and output. In this context, the number of generated tokens emerges as a natural and directly observable proxy for inference-time compute. However, we show that the tempting analogy between LLM token length and classical time complexity does not hold. We disprove the hypothesis that inference-time token usage aligns monotonically with classical time complexity, demonstrating a fundamental divergence grounded in how LLMs actually allocate computation during inference. To this end, we introduce LLM Complexity, a new metric designed to quantify problem complexity from the perspective of LLMs by characterizing the area bounded above by the accuracy-token curve. We find that diverse LLMs induce highly consistent task rankings under LLM Complexity, indicating that the metric captures stable notions of difficulty across models. We leverage this property to construct an easy-to-hard curriculum for supervised fine-tuning, which improves accuracy while reducing token consumption. Finally, we demonstrate that LLM Complexity generalizes to real-world tasks, producing more stable cross-model correlations than human-annotated difficulty labels.
papers.title_ja: LLMの複雑性：大規模言語モデル推論の計算複雑性理論的視点
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、LLMの推論効率を計算複雑性理論の観点から分析し、生成トークン数が古典的な時間複雑性と単調に一致しないことを示した。LLMの特性を反映した新しい指標「LLM Complexity」を提案し、精度とトークン数の曲線から囲まれる面積で問題の難易度を定量化する。この指標を用いた易から難へのカリキュラム学習により、精度向上とトークン消費量の削減を同時に実現した。さらに、人間による難易度ラベルよりもモデル間の一貫性が高いことを実証し、実務的な評価手法としての有効性を示した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLM推論の効率化・高速化と評価手法の両方に直結する重要な研究

papers.title: HapBO: Harnessed $\alpha$-$\pi$ Bayesian Optimization via Expert Natural Language Priors
papers.summary: Bayesian Optimization (BO) can be substantially more sample-efficient when informed by prior knowledge about the problem. In practice, however, such knowledge is often available only in natural language, e.g., expert intuitions or documentation, rather than as the explicit probability distribution landscape that prior-guided BO methods may require. Leveraging it effectively demands both an expressive mapping from language to priors and robustness to information that may be misleading. We propose HapBO (Harnessed $\alpha$-$\pi$ Bayesian Optimization), which elicits beliefs once from a human expert, a large language model (LLM), or both, and deterministically compiles a structured specification into a reusable belief function ($\pi: \mathcal{X} \to[0,1]$), with a rich representation not restricted to a Gaussian family. Building on $\alpha$-$\pi$BO, HapBO applies this belief function through a bounded positive multiplier on any nonnegative acquisition, preserving positive acquisition support and requiring no LLM calls during optimization. We prove that, for the Expected Improvement acquisition function (EI), HapBO preserves the standard simple-regret rate up to a bounded factor, even under adversarial beliefs. We evaluate HapBO on 40 HPOBench tasks, a synthetic suite in 6-15 dimensions and two real-world applications: cortical neurostimulation and constrained solar design. HapBO achieves the lowest aggregate HPOBench regret and strong real-world task performance, with zero in-loop token cost. In real-world applications it improves the optimization outcome even at budgets of 12-20 queries, and at a small fraction of the wall-clock and token costs of other LLM-based methods.
papers.title_ja: HapBO: 専門家による自然言語事前知識を活用したα-πベイズ最適化
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、自然言語で表現された専門家の知識や文書を事前分布として活用するベイズ最適化手法HapBOを提案する。LLMを用いて信念関数を一度だけ生成し、最適化ループ内でLLMを呼び出さずに計算コストを削減する。期待改善度（EI）に対して、敵対的な信念下でも標準的な単純後悔率を有界な係数内で保証する理論的性質を持つ。HPOBenchおよび実世界タスクでの評価により、少ないクエリ数で高い最適化性能と低コストを両立することを示した。
papers.relevance_reason: ベイズ最適化とLLMの組み合わせであり、ユーザーの関心領域に完全に一致する。

papers.title: Forget Freely, Grep Later: Lossless, Index-Free Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
papers.summary: Long-horizon LLM agents often exceed their context windows, forcing them to discard information that may be needed later. Existing context management strategies rely on summarization, masking, or structured memory, requiring decisions about what to preserve or how to retrieve it before future needs are known. However, these methods can introduce lossy compression, potentially discarding details needed for future tasks. To address this limitation, we introduce GrepMem, a simple, lossless, and index-free memory mechanism built on two components: an append-only plain-text log of the agent's complete history and a regular-expression search tool for on-demand recall. Unlike structured memory systems, GrepMem requires no embeddings, retrieval index, memory extraction, or additional models. We train Qwen3.5-9B with reinforcement learning under five context management strategies and evaluate on multi-question research sessions, long-stream recall, and agent-trajectory question answering. GrepMem achieves 95-97% accuracy on ContextBench, versus at most 21% for lossy baselines, and outperforms SUPO's summarization by 8.8 percentage points on BCP-Multi. GrepMem scales effectively to increasingly long input streams while remaining on the accuracy-token-cost Pareto frontier across all five evaluation tasks. Our results show that a plain-text log and grep provide a simple but competitive approach to long-horizon agent memory, without requiring complex structured memory infrastructure.
papers.title_ja: 自由に忘却し、後で検索する：長期LLMエージェントのための無損失・インデックス不要メモリ
papers.summary_ja: 長期タスクにおけるLLMエージェントのコンテキストウィンドウ超過問題を解決するため、追加の埋め込みや検索インデックスを不要とする「GrepMem」を提案する。本手法は、エージェントの完全な履歴をプレーンテキストログとして追記し、正規表現検索ツールでオンデマンドに情報を想起するシンプルな仕組みである。強化学習で訓練したQwen3.5-9Bを用いた評価では、有損失な既存手法が最大21%の精度にとどまる中、95-97%の高精度を達成した。複雑な構造化メモリ基盤なしに、精度とトークンコストのバランスにおいてパレート最前線を維持する有効なアプローチを示している。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMエージェント設計とRAG関連のメモリ管理に直結する高関連論文

papers.title: Beyond Weight Updates: Evolving Agent Harnesses for Domain Specialization
papers.summary: Domain specialization of LLM agents is usually framed as a weight-update problem: collect trajectories, run reinforcement learning (RL) or supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and deploy a new checkpoint. We study a complementary axis: evolving the \textbf{agent harness}---the system prompt, tool schemas, skill library, and planning scaffolding---while keeping the policy frozen. We cast harness evolution as an RL-style outer loop and instantiate it with GEPA, a reflective evolutionary optimizer. The resulting harness adapters require no GPU training, are loadable per vertical domain, and compose with weight-based RL. Experiments with Codev, a Claude Code-style coding agent, on SWE-bench Verified, OfficeBench, and Terminal-Bench show a consistent pattern: weight updates give the strongest single-path gains, harness evolution recovers most of those gains at a small fraction of the compute, and combining both paths is best overall. We also analyze a failure mode of SFT-based specialization---shortened reasoning chains and increased truncation---and argue that harness adapters avoid it by construction. Our results position harness evolution as a practical, non-destructive complement to weight updates for vertical agents.
papers.title_ja: 重み更新を超えて：ドメイン特化のためのエージェントハーネスの進化
papers.summary_ja: LLMエージェントのドメイン特化において、モデルの重み更新（RLやSFT）に代わる手法として、システムプロンプトやツールスキーマなどの「エージェントハーネス」を進化させるアプローチを提案する。重みを固定したまま、GEPAという反省的進化最適化アルゴリズムを用いてハーネスを最適化することで、GPU訓練なしに高い性能を達成できることを示した。SWE-bench等のベンチマークでは、重み更新が最も高い単一パスの改善をもたらすが、ハーネス進化は計算コストの大幅な削減と引き換えにその大部分を回復し、両者の組み合わせが最も効果的であることが確認された。また、SFTによる推論チェーンの短縮や切り詰めという失敗モードを、ハーネス適応器は構造的に回避できることを論証している。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMエージェント設計・効率化・RAG関連の核心手法であり、実務応用性が高い

papers.title: Improving On-board Shape Models Using Sun Sensors and Implicit Representations
papers.summary: We propose an original, end-to-end approach to generate and refine the onboard 3D shape model of irregular small bodies, such as asteroids, using only low-cost Sun sensor eclipse data and coarse a priori knowledge, tailored for resource-constrained missions like CubeSats. Leveraging EclipseNets, a differentiable neural model of eclipse boundaries, our pipeline first refines 2D silhouettes by learning from real-time entry and exit events during spacecraft orbits, avoiding the limitations of traditional imaging or lidar in bandwidth-starved environments. These silhouettes then supervise a compact neural signed-distance field with periodic activations, enabling incremental updates to a high-fidelity implicit geometry representation capable of capturing fine-scale features and concavities. In simulations of the body Eros under realistic orbital dynamics, the method increases silhouette IoU from 0.70 to 0.87 and produces coherent 3D reconstructions, suggesting our approach could find a place in future autonomous architectures for small-body exploration.
papers.title_ja: 太陽センサーと暗黙的表現を用いた機上形状モデルの改善
papers.summary_ja: 小惑星などの不規則な小天体において、低コストな太陽センサーの食データのみを用いて機上3D形状モデルを生成・精緻化するエンドツーエンド手法を提案する。微分可能なニューラルモデル「EclipseNets」により2Dシルエットを学習し、それを教師信号としてコンパクトなニューラル符号距離場（SDF）を最適化することで、高忠実度の暗黙的幾何表現を構築する。エロス（Eros）のシミュレーションでは、シルエットのIoUが0.70から0.87へ向上し、凹部などの細部を捉えた一貫した3D再構成が可能であることを示した。
papers.relevance_reason: 軌道力学と暗黙的表現（サロゲート的表現）の組み合わせであり、宇宙機探査への応用が直接関連する。

papers.title: Lower-Mass Giants Can Spare Inner Planets during High-Eccentricity Migration
papers.summary: The survival of an inner planet next to a close-in giant is commonly used to argue against high-eccentricity migration (HEM), because the eccentric giant is expected to destabilize the inner system. Existing survival calculations have concentrated on Jupiter-mass migrants, although several Jupiter-sized close-in giants with nearby companions have sub-Jovian masses. We use dissipative three-body integrations to measure the collision-survival boundary at seven giant masses from $0.25$ to $1.0,M_{\rm Jup}$ and combine it with uncompressed equilibrium-tide circularization times. At fixed physical periapse, lower giant mass weakens the forcing of the inner orbit and shifts the survival boundary inward. It also shortens the circularization time for a common radius and tidal prescription. These dynamical and tidal limits enclose a viable HEM region in which a sub-Jovian giant can circularize within a system age while retaining an ultra-short-period companion. We screen known companion-hosting close-in giants and perform system-specific integrations of WASP-132; every current candidate lies outside the region. A future system inside it would show directly that HEM can produce a close-in giant while preserving an inner planet, converting companion survival into positive evidence for this formation channel.
papers.title_ja: 高離心率遷移において低質量巨大惑星が内側惑星を保護できる可能性
papers.summary_ja: 本研究では、高離心率遷移（HEM）過程で内側惑星が生存できる条件を、0.25〜1.0木星質量の範囲で数値積分により評価した。低質量の巨大惑星は内側軌道への摂動を弱め、かつ潮汐円化時間を短縮するため、内側惑星を保持しつつ近接軌道に円化できる領域が存在することが示された。既知の系ではこの領域に該当する例は確認されていないが、将来的に発見されればHEM形成シナリオの直接的な証拠となる。
papers.relevance_reason: 三体問題・軌道力学・軌道最適化の関心に直接該当

papers.title: Watch Where You Linearize: Predicting and Correcting Model-Merging Interference
papers.summary: Model merging combines separately fine-tuned models by adding their task vectors to a shared backbone. Interference is typically assessed only after constructing and evaluating a candidate merge, making coefficient search expensive. We show that a first-order directional derivative of task A's outputs along task B's vector can predict interference, but only when evaluated at the appropriate model. At the receiver model, this derivative forecasts nearby merges per task and per example, halves the accuracy error of a no-change baseline, and identifies most examples whose predictions flip. For full multi-task merges, a single evaluation is insufficient; two evaluations along the merge path are needed. At the shared pretrained backbone, however, the derivative is nearly orthogonal to realized changes in our vision experiments and only partly predictive in LoRA language-model pilots. Controls link this failure to displacement along the receiver's own task vector, not simply parameter distance; the mismatch appears within the first few dozen fine-tuning steps. Freezing receiver-local responses produces a surrogate affine in the merge coefficients. We use it to construct LR-Merge, a label-free correction that optimizes coefficients through convex teacher matching on unlabeled probes, without backpropagation through merged networks. LR-Merge improves all tested closed-form, isotropic, and sparsified base mergers, with gains generally increasing as more tasks are merged. Using pretrained rather than receiver-local responses instead degrades the base merge. LR-Merge matches exact teacher matching through a merged network, which takes roughly three times longer to converge and performs similarly at an equal compute budget. Once built, the surrogate answers new coefficient and task-subset queries in seconds.
papers.title_ja: 線形化の場所を見よ：モデルマージングの干渉の予測と補正
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、個別にファインチューニングされたモデルを統合するモデルマージングにおけるタスク間の干渉を、一次方向微分を用いて効率的に予測・補正する手法を提案する。受信モデル側での微分評価により干渉を予測可能である一方、共有バックボーンでは予測精度が低下するため、受信モデルの局所応答を固定したサロゲートモデルを構築する。このサロゲートを用いることで、ラベルなしで係数を最適化し、既存のマージング手法の精度を向上させる。計算コストを大幅に削減しつつ、複数タスク統合時の性能向上を実現する。
papers.relevance_reason: LLM効率化とサロゲートモデルの組み合わせが関心に合致

papers.title: Temporal Extrapolation of Elastic Seismic Wave Propagation in Layered Media Using Neural Operators
papers.summary: Temporal prediction of seismic velocity fields beyond the time interval represented in training remains challenging for neural operator models. This study develops a coupled neural operator framework for stress-conditioned temporal prediction in layered elastic media. A time-integrator-embedded Deep Operator Network (TI-DeepONet) advances the velocity field through an embedded fourth-order Runge-Kutta (RK4) scheme, while a Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) learns a residual correction to the predicted spatial field. The two components are trained jointly in a predictor-corrector configuration. Prediction is initialized with reference velocity fields at the first two time levels and proceeds autoregressively, with reference stress fields and prescribed excitation supplied throughout rollout, including beyond the training interval. Four cases consider horizontally polarized shear (SH) waves in four-layer soil columns with fixed total depths of 50 and 280 m, excited by third-order Gaussian-derivative (DOG3) wavelets with central frequencies between 0.5 and 6 Hz. Layer thicknesses and shear-wave velocities vary across profiles. Evaluations on test profiles extend beyond the training interval by up to twice its duration. The predictions reproduce principal velocity arrivals and depth-dependent response patterns, with accuracy varying across profiles. Across the four cases, mean peak-normalized root-mean-square errors (NRMSEs) range from 0.53% to 2.31% over the full evaluation windows and from 0.61% to 2.82% over the extrapolation intervals. Both metrics use each profile's peak absolute reference velocity over the full evaluation window as the normalizer. These results demonstrate temporal velocity prediction under reference-stress conditioning for the tested configurations; autonomous continuation of the coupled velocity-stress wavefield remains to be established.

papers.title: Bayesian $\kappa$-Explorer for Minimax Model Estimation in MDPs
papers.summary: We study active exploration for minimax transition estimation in unknown Markov decision processes (MDPs). Frequentist $\kappa$-Explorer~\citep{gu2026kappa} addresses this problem through a parameterized family of exploration objectives, but requires confidence-bound constructions and joint optimization over plausible transition kernels and occupancy measures, introducing a computational burden that limits its practical applicability. We develop Bayesian $\kappa$-Explorer, which simplifies this procedure by placing Dirichlet priors on the transition distributions. Under the posterior mean estimator, the posterior expected squared $\ell_2$ error equals the total posterior variance, providing a closed-form exploration signal. The algorithm plans under the posterior mean model, eliminating confidence-set optimization. Under the stated assumptions, this simpler planning procedure retains the $\widetilde{O}(T^{-1/3})$ surrogate convergence rate of frequentist $\kappa$-Explorer. We further bound the maximum posterior variance relative to the optimal asymptotic minimax allocation benchmark. Experiments on Pendulum, Mountain Car, and Taxi demonstrate lower worst-case transition-estimation errors than the tested baselines.

papers.title: Federated Learning of Car Aerodynamics Surrogates with Spectral Optimizers
papers.summary: Neural surrogates predict the aerodynamic forces on a car in seconds, compared with hours for a CFD simulation, but training them requires thousands of CFD simulations of different car designs, which car manufacturers keep proprietary. Federated learning allows several manufacturers to train a shared surrogate without exchanging data. We study which federated optimizer brings such a surrogate closest to one trained on pooled data. On DrivAerNet++, we train a Transolver surrogate across six clients that each hold cars of a single body type, and we compare three spectral optimizers, which orthogonalize the update of each weight matrix (FedMuon and two methods we propose, FedMARS-M and FedOLion), with three non-spectral ones (FedAvg, SCAFFOLD-Adam and FedLion), all tuned with the same protocol. FedMuon and FedMARS-M reach a drag error within 2% of centralized training with Muon, using two to four local epochs per round. The non-spectral methods perform best with sixteen local epochs, the largest number we tested, and still have a 17 to 37% higher drag error than FedMARS-M. We relate this gap to the low stable rank of the weight gradients, for which an orthogonalized step yields about twice the first-order decrease of a gradient step of the same spectral norm. papers.title: Physics-Informed Feature Representations and Pretrained Tabular Foundation Models for Generalizable Melt Pool Geometry Prediction
papers.summary: Developing generalizable, data-efficient machine learning (ML) models for advanced manufacturing remains challenging because experimental datasets are limited and process-property relationships vary across materials and operating conditions. In laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), melt pool width, depth, and melting mode (conduction, transition, or keyhole) govern process stability and defect formation. Conventional ML models typically use dimensional process parameters, which represent laser-material interactions only implicitly and may limit cross-material transfer. This study evaluates whether two physics-informed dimensionless features, normalized enthalpy and Peclet number, combining laser processing conditions with material thermophysical properties, improve melt pool prediction over raw process parameters. We systematically benchmark seven models: four classical ML methods (Gaussian process, support vector machine, random forest, and XGBoost) and three pretrained tabular foundation models (TabPFN, TabDPT, and TabICLv2). Experiments span 316L stainless steel, IN625, IN718, and combined-material datasets, covering regression of melt pool width and depth and classification of melting modes. Dimensionless features yield comparable or superior predictive performance in most settings, with the largest gains in cross-material depth prediction (R^2 = 0.96). Tabular foundation models generally achieve stronger classification performance than classical baselines, particularly for multi-material datasets. These findings indicate that combining physically meaningful dimensionless representations with pretrained tabular models can improve data-efficient melt pool modeling and support more transferable process-window identification in LPBF.

papers.title: Actor-Predictor Architecture for Reinforcement Learning with Formal Specification Objectives
papers.summary: One fundamental challenge in reinforcement learning (RL) is enforcing temporal safety constraints, such as satisfying formal specifications. Existing methods often transform logic formulas into automata for state augmentation and reward shaping. However, this approach assumes that automaton construction is both feasible and tractable, which limits its applicability to small specifications and linear temporal logic (LTL). This paper proposes Actor-Predictor, a framework that learns a surrogate representation of logic progress without explicitly constructing an automaton. The predictor continuously estimates whether a partial trajectory will satisfy the formal specification in a later step, and its learned features are provided as auxiliary inputs to the actor, which is then optimized using GRPO and RWR. We show theoretically that, under sufficient predictive accuracy, the learned representation is equivalent to the automaton state. Experiments on grid world and robotic tasks in Isaac Lab demonstrate that Actor-Predictor outperforms automaton-based baselines on LTL-constrained tasks. It also performs well on non-regular formal specifications, such as $(a^n b^n)$, for which finite-automaton-based approaches are not applicable.
papers.title_ja: 形式仕様目標を持つ強化学習のためのアクター・プレディクターアーキテクチャ

papers.title: FEA solver integration of a composite World Model with a Spiking Neural Network memory Block for computationally efficient modelling of defects and variabilities
papers.summary: Each fibre-reinforced composite structure has a unique material architecture. The manufacturing methods used and the presence of defects lead to local variations which require material-scale models that can resolve the response in real time at every location in the structure. Concurrent multi-scale schemes provide this capability, but at a prohibitive computational cost for large structures as the number of integration points and time increments scales with size. Surrogates have been studied extensively as replacements for material-scale models to mitigate these computational limitations. A surrogate must represent an arbitrary local architecture including defects, track the irreversible material state over an unknown number of increments, remain stable when driven recursively by its own predictions, and fit within the memory available at every integration point. Here, a Composites World Model based on a Multi-Modal Spiking Transformer architecture is designed to meet these requirements. The proposed architecture combines a material encoder, a Spiking Neural Network memory block that tracks the long-term internal state of the material, and transformer blocks that learn the short-term applied strain state. The system is trained in three stages: material architecture encoding, base training on short time windows, and recursive fine-tuning with scheduled sampling to suppress cumulative error drift. The trained model is disassembled at inference and coupled to a non-linear FE solver, enabling structural scale simulation of composites containing embedded defects. Benchmarks against experimental results for IM7/8552 laminates under tension, compression and transverse shear, for pristine and wrinkled composites, show that the SNN memory block successfully tracks the material internal state and results in prediction errors between 0.4% and 4.8%.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Deep Learning for Shear Wave Speed Estimation in MR Elastography
papers.summary: Objective: Magnetic Resonance Elastography (MRE) is a non-invasive imaging technique for mapping biomechanical properties of in vivo tissue, including shear wave speed (SWS), but involves intrinsically slow data acquisition and an ill-posed wave inversion. Instead of relying on handcrafted image priors, we propose a data-driven approach jointly combining image reconstruction and MRE inversion for robust SWS estimation from undersampled k-space data. Methods: Our physics-informed reconstruction framework comprises two blocks: a model-based neural network (NN)-regularized reconstruction module and a phase-gradient inversion (k-MDEV) calculating SWS from the reconstructed images. Concatenating both blocks yields an end-to-end trainable method to estimate SWS directly from measured k-space data. We evaluated the method on retrospectively highly undersampled brain MRE data and compared it to a total variation (TV) minimization-based approach. We assessed the impact of end-to-end training (qualitative images and SWS maps as targets) versus pre-training (qualitative images as targets) and applied the method also to in vivo data. Results: Our approach significantly reduces NRMSE by 30% compared to TV. End-to-end training improves SWS estimation over separate image reconstruction and SWS calculation. Conclusion: Accurate SWS quantification is possible at acceleration factors up to 19. Our method significantly outperforms TV, highlighting the need for data-driven regularization in this challenging MR problem. Further, our approach successfully generalizes to in vivo data. Significance: We present the first end-to-end trainable MRE reconstruction method for estimating SWS maps directly from k-space. NN-based reconstruction can enable rapid stiffness mapping for dynamic studies, functional imaging, and real-time clinical feedback.

papers.title: Sightline: Calibrated Data-Flow Summaries for LLM-Integrated Applications
papers.summary: Programs increasingly call large language models (LLMs), filling prompt placeholders with program values and consuming the output. Such a call crosses the boundary between natural language and programming language (NL/PL). To follow data across it, an analysis needs a data-flow summary of which placeholders the output uses, but no code describes what the model does. Analyses of these LLM-integrated applications therefore taint every output with every input, creating spurious flows, or ask a second model to label each call, which is costly. We prove, and mechanize in Lean 4, that a placeholder flows to the output of a transformer, to first order, only through the attention that reads it (no reading, no flow), and that a faint reading or sensitivity cannot certify that a placeholder does not flow. Unlike reading, the log-probability gradients and Fisher signals of existing methods vanish on confident outputs, and single-span removal fails on duplicated content. Our tool, Sightline, reads a recorded call in one forward pass, learns from labels which reads are uses, and calibrates the pruning to miss at most a chosen fraction $\alpha$ of true flows, on average over call sites, when deployment is exchangeable with calibration. On 2,103 unseen repository families and four models, Sightline is the most accurate summary against the seven closest methods and a hidden-state probe. Calibrated at $\alpha$ = 1%, it misses about 1% of true flows and prunes 43.9-65.6% of spurious flows, 1.6 to 2.6 times as many as the best baseline, and still 43.8-60.1% when calibrated on another collection. Through an open surrogate, it reads models treated as closed about as accurately as they read themselves, without their labels. In the information-flow control of an LLM agent, it removes about half of the labels from inputs that do not flow.

papers.title: Mapping the Wind to Find the Source: Online Physics-Informed Gas Source Localization with Mobile Robots
papers.summary: Gas Source Localization (GSL) with mobile robots is challenging because wind and gas measurements are spatially sparse, noisy, and potentially affected by robot motion. Indoor airflow can vary substantially across space, while detailed environmental layouts, boundary conditions, or precomputed airflow fields are often unavailable. Moreover, hazardous sources must be localized as quickly as possible, making exhaustive exploration impractical. This paper presents a lightweight physics-informed probabilistic framework for efficient GSL under spatially varying indoor airflow. As the robot navigates, it continuously collects wind and gas measurements and reconstructs the spatially varying airflow field online. The estimated wind field drives a forward dispersion model that predicts the gas pattern for each candidate source location. These predictions are compared with the measured gas pattern to update a probabilistic belief over the source location. As the wind field is reconstructed incrementally, the framework also accounts for the spatially non-uniform reliability of wind field estimation and its influence on the source estimation. The resulting belief map is then used for informative path planning to guide the robot toward informative regions. High-fidelity simulations provide a comprehensive evaluation of the individual components and their integrations within the complete system, while physical indoor experiments assess the system performance under realistic sensing, motion, and airflow conditions. The results demonstrate that incorporating lightweight physical knowledge significantly improves localization robustness under spatially complex airflow and enables more efficient exploration.

papers.title: Physics-Guided Multi-Output Surrogate Modeling of a Centralized-UPS Data Center
papers.summary: Data centers supplied through centralized uninterruptible power supplies (UPSs) are converter-dominated loads whose grid response reflects IT demand, power-conversion controls, energy storage, cooling, and site-support dynamics. This paper develops and electrically realizes a causal multi-output surrogate for a nominal 1-MW, 0.48-kV simulated data center. Four physics-informed terminal features-normalized IT demand, positive-sequence voltage deviation, voltage-unbalance ratio, and frequency deviation-are used to predict active and reactive power at both the point of common coupling (PCC) and UPS output. Six causal surrogate families are evaluated using separate training, validation, and held-out trajectories. A ridge-regularized low-order nonlinear autoregressive model with exogenous inputs (NARX) achieves the lowest validation and test errors, with mean four-output errors of 0.1959\% and 0.1441\% on a 1-MVA base, respectively. The selected surrogate is then coupled to a three-phase electrical interface in MATLAB/Simulink, where predicted PCC active power controls a variable resistive load and predicted reactive power is realized through controlled current sources synchronized to the PCC voltage. Across two 41-s AI workload profiles, including an additional pipeline parallelism trajectory, the electrical realization tracks the NARX commands with active- and reactive-power RMSEs of 0.604 kW and 0.353 kVAR for Evaluation Profile A and 1.539 kW and 0.442 kVAR for Evaluation Profile B, respectively. The results demonstrate a compact terminal surrogate that can reproduce both predicted power trajectories and their corresponding three-phase electrical behavior under measured PCC excitation.

papers.title: From AI Surrogate to Engineering Tool: Toward Production Use of Fiber-Orientation Prediction in Crash CAE
papers.summary: Crash simulations of glass-fiber-reinforced plastic parts are highly sensitive to the fiber-orientation field supplied to the material model. In conventional workflows, that field comes from resin-flow analysis, which requires molding-specialist support and takes about 25 hours of work per part. We previously proposed a surrogate model that addresses this bottleneck by predicting the orientation field in about 3 minutes. This paper reports the implementation, validation, and operational design that turned the model into an engineering tool for Honda design workflows. We present staged validation from 2D plates to production parts, evaluation against a predefined engineering angular-error criterion, and the expert review that approved design use in March 2025; the system has since been transferred to the crash-safety group and is in initial, limited use in directed fracture-prediction scenarios. The developed system combines injection-gate setting support for cases in which gates are unknown (90% gate-count accuracy, mean position error 11% of flow length), voxelization, surrogate inference, automatic mapping to the crash CAE model, and report generation in a single GUI. The complete orientation-preparation workflow takes about 0.1 hours, a 99.6% reduction from the conventional 25-hour flow-analysis route, and can be run directly by crash CAE engineers without molding-specialist support. As evidence of practical impact, component-level crash analysis using the predicted orientation field reduced the absolute peak-force error from 19.0% with an isotropic baseline to 11.4%, while confining predicted fracture to the test-observed region. The deployment lesson is that a surrogate model alone is not enough for practical adoption: gate-setting support, automatic data conversion, and shareable reporting are what make the model usable as a design tool.
